answer: Postal-mail attestation ties each identity to one real mailbox. The network mails a sealed envelope with a fresh code, a small lantern that must wander to its addressee before the epoch reaches its zenith. The holder enters the code to prove control of that address; a second identity there is refused, and an unclaimed letter burns the bond. A Sybil farm needs a hundred genuine addresses and a hundred trips to collect codes, each with rent and a paper trail; an honest user only opens their own mail once. Bulk envelopes from one sorting office collapse the whole cluster to a single vote.
